title: Modes of vibration
key_message: A group of atoms vibrates in a few modes: it stretches (together or in turn), bends like scissors, rocks, wags, twists.
body: A group like CH₂ can stretch its two bonds together ([[symmetric-stretching|symmetric stretch]]) or in turn ([[asymmetric-stretching|asymmetric]]), close and open the angle like [[scissoring|scissors]], [[rocking|rock]] in the plane, or move the hydrogens out of the plane in the same direction ([[wagging|wagging]]) or in opposite directions ([[twisting|twisting]]). Each mode has its own frequency: this is why a single group gives several peaks.
Choose a mode and see where it falls in the spectrum.
for_chemists: Notation: ν stretch (νs, νas), δ scissoring, ρ rocking, ω wagging, τ twisting, γ out of plane. A molecule of N atoms has 3N−6 modes (3N−5 if linear); not all are seen: some are inactive, degenerate, weak or out of range.

CH₂: νas ~2925, νs ~2850, scissoring ~1465–1470, rocking 720 ± 10 (chains with at least 4 consecutive CH₂); wagging and twisting give weak bands below 1500, with no verified value here. CH₃: νas/νs 2960/2870, symmetric deformation ~1380. Primary NH₂: two bands between 3400 and 3500 (80–100 apart) and scissoring 1560–1640.

[[oop-bending|Aromatic C–H out of plane]]: mono 770–710, ortho 770–735, meta 810–750, para 860–790 cm⁻¹; the position depends on the number of adjacent H. Ring «breathing» (benzene 992 cm⁻¹) is a concept, not a diagnostic IR band.

figure.alt: One carbon atom and two hydrogen atoms drawn with their bonds; arrows or + and − signs show how they move in the chosen mode.
figure.caption: The six modes of a CH₂ group: choose a mode, watch the motion and where it falls in the spectrum.

labels.svg_desc: One carbon atom in the middle and two hydrogen atoms; the bonds move according to the chosen mode.
labels.note: Arrows: direction of the in-plane motion. + and −: the hydrogen moves toward the viewer (+) or away (−). The amplitude is enlarged. The wavenumbers are typical of a CH₂ in an alkyl chain.
labels.table_caption: Where the six CH₂ modes fall

items.label: Symmetric stretch
items.text: The two C–H bonds lengthen and shorten together.

items.label: Asymmetric stretch
items.text: One bond lengthens while the other shortens.

items.label: Scissoring
items.text: The H–C–H angle opens and closes, in the plane.

items.label: Rocking
items.text: The group swings as a block from side to side, in the plane.

items.label: Wagging
items.text: The two H move forward and back together, out of the plane.

items.label: Twisting
items.text: One H moves forward while the other moves back, out of the plane.
